Entries.Text: Select a behavior file (Behavior category) to browse it here.
Select a behavior file (Behavior category) to see its state machines here.
The behavior as a tree of its state machines, states and generators. Right-click a node for Add Animation, Clone State and Add Transition.
One row per animation selector (CMSG), with its animation ID, state, clips, and what the character has for it.
Every state machine in the file.
Every animation selector (CMSG) in the file.
Every animation clip in the file.
The behavior's variables, with the bindings that use each one. Add Variable is here.
Mistakes that make the game crash or silently do nothing: missing indices, mismatched lists, duplicate state IDs, broken bindings.
Back to the state machine this one was opened from.
Select something in a state machine to show it.

Show the state machine of whatever is selected in the Outline.

In the graph: links are transitions from one state to another (hover for their events). Wildcard transitions, which can be taken from any state, are listed on the state they lead to (* events). Double-click a state whose generator is a state machine to open it. Drag from a state's Out to another state to add a transition.
Reached from any state on {0} events:

Add a clip to this selector for another animation category (aCCC_ plus the selector's animation ID). The clip copies one of the selector's clips, and is given an animation name entry if the animation is new to the file.
Copy this state into the same state machine, with a new name and state ID. Its transitions out are copied; transitions into it aren't.
Add a transition to a state on an event, from one state or from any state (a wildcard transition). The event can be a new one.
Add a variable, with its info, bounds and initial value kept in step.
The animation category: the aCCC in aCCC_YYYYYY. For the player, each category has its own time act (a000, a020 ...).

Off: generators also used outside this state stay shared, so the copy refers to the same ones (an edit to them changes both).
On: everything below the state is copied.

Transition effects always stay shared.
A wildcard transition can be taken from any state of the machine, and is how most of the game's transitions are made.
The variable's value when the behavior starts.
Starts at zero (vector, quaternion as identity) or null (pointer). Edit it afterwards in the Variables tab.
This file has no behavior graph data to add to.
This selector has no generator list.
This selector already has a clip for {0}.
There's no clip in this file to copy.

{0} isn't used by any clip in this behavior yet, and this behbnd has no character file animation list (Characters/cXXXX.hkx, m_animationBundleNameData) to add it to. In this game that list names every animation the behavior plays; where the behbnd has one, new animations are added to it automatically.
This file has no animation names to add the new animation to.
The state's state machine wasn't found.
The state machine already has a state called {0}.
Pick an event, or enter a new one.
The object isn't referenced from there any more.
Remove this reference to the selected object. It's still used in {0} other places. Can be undone.

Remove this reference to the selected object. It's the only one, so the object leaves the file. Can be undone.

Removing a state leaves any transitions to it pointing at a missing state; the Problems tab lists those.

What {0} has for {1}: a time act entry (its events), and an animation file in its anibnds.

A missing one isn't always a mistake. Shared graphs like c9997 name animations most characters don't have, and the game skips those.
Show {0} in the Time Act Editor.
No time act entry has this ID
The animations of {0} with a time act entry for this ID. With an offset type other than None, the game picks the category at runtime (from the weapon, stance or magic), so any of these can play.
Only show selectors with a clip whose animation file this character doesn't have.

Click to edit this selector. Double-click to show it in the Outline.

Time Acts: the categories with a time act entry for the animation ID.
Files: the clips whose animation file this character has.

Check the file again.

Checked: event, variable, character property and state indices; the lengths of the lists kept alongside the name lists; duplicate state IDs; clip internal IDs against their animation names; binding member paths.

The game's own files pass every check, so anything listed comes from an edit.

On: {0}

Click to show it in the Outline.
State ID {0} is used by more than one state: {1}
m_animationInternalId {0} is past the end of the animation names ({1})
Binding "{0}" doesn't lead to a field: {1}
Go back to the previously selected node.
Go forward again after going back.

This object is referenced from {0} places, so it's shown under each of them. An edit to it changes it everywhere it's used.

The Used By list shows where.
The objects that reference the selected object, with the field each one holds it in. Click one to show it in the Outline.
Select this object in the Outline tab, with the tree opened down to it.

This object isn't shown in the Outline itself, so the Outline shows the node above it:
{0}
The {0} this number refers to. Pick another here, or edit the number in the row above.
No {0} has the index {1} in this file, so the game won't find it.
No state machine found above this object.
The variable's name, at index {0} in the behavior graph's variable names.
The variable's initial word value. For vector and pointer variables, this is the index of its value in the quad or variant value list.
The objects whose fields are set from this variable.
Copy this and what's below it. A copy held by a state goes into a new state of the same state machine; a copy held by a selector's list goes at the end of that list.
Remove this from every place that holds it. If a state holds it, the state is deleted too, with the transitions into that state.
Drive one of this object's fields from a behavior variable.
Stop a field of this object being driven by a variable or character property.
Add a copy of the selected variable (type, bounds and initial value) at the end of the list. Its bindings aren't copied.
Remove the selected variable and the bindings to it. The variables after it move down one, and every index to them follows.
This object has no fields a variable can drive.
The field the variable sets. Fields that are already bound show their binding. Fields inside sub-objects (such as hands:0/controlData) can be bound in the property grid.
A {0} variable may not suit a {1} field.
This field is already bound: its binding will be changed to this variable.
The copy's m_animId. If it changes, the selector's clips are copied and pointed at the new animation (same categories).
Its clips will be copied and pointed at animation {0}.
The copy goes at the end of the list, so the other entries keep their indices.
The copy is added at index {0}.
{0} field(s) that name it are set to -1
The {0} variable(s) after it move down one index; the bindings to them follow
Scripts (HKS), other behavior files and the game may use this variable by name. Those aren't checked.
Removed from {0} (entry {1}); the {2} entries after it move down one, so selector indices to them change
State {0} is deleted from {1}, with {2} transition(s) into it
it's held by {0}.{1} (only states and selector lists are supported)
it's inside {0}, which is used in {1} places
no state or selector list was found above it
The clip's animation name {0} isn't aXXX_YYYYYY, so it can't be pointed at the new ID.
{0} is its state machine's only state.
{0} is the start state of {1}. Change the start state first.
Copy this clip into its selector for another category (aCCC_ of the selector's animation ID). A selector's clips each have their own category.
The category of the copy. It starts at the one after the selector's highest; a category the selector already has can't be used.
Remove this clip from every selector that holds it.
it isn't held by a selector
Copy for Paste. Clips, selectors and state machines can only be pasted into the file they were copied from.
Copy this variable for Paste. It can be pasted into any behavior file.

Clips go into the selected selector (or the selected clip's selector) for their category, or the next free one. Selectors and state machines go where the selected selector or state machine is held, as Duplicate would place them. Variables go at the end of the variable list.
Clips, selectors and state machines can only be pasted into the file they were copied from.
The copied variable is from another Havok version.
{0}: select a selector (CMSG) or a clip to paste a clip into.
{0}: select a selector or state machine to paste next to.
The behavior file whose selectors get the clips. An enemy's selectors are usually in the shared c9997.hkx; the player's are in c0000.hkx.
{0} animations: {1} to add, {2} already registered, {3} with a category their selectors don't use, {4} with no selector.
Animations no selector of this file plays (no selector has their ID). They'd need a new state and selector, which Register doesn't create.
Also add to selectors whose offset type doesn't use the category

A selector plays the category its offset type gives (weapon, sword art, magic, idle ...). By default a clip is only added where another selector with the same offset type already has that category. Tick this for a category that is new to the file, such as a new weapon category.
{0} isn't in the character's anibnds. The clip can still be added, but the game will have nothing to play.
Selectors with this animation ID lack the clip for this category.
Every selector that uses this category already has the clip.
Selectors have this animation ID, but no selector of their offset type has a clip of this category in this file, so the game may never pick it. Tick the row to add it anyway.
No selector of this file has this animation ID (selectors without clips are ignored).
The selectors with this animation ID:
skipped: no {0} selector uses category {1} (added if forced)
Register in Behavior: added {0} clips for {1} ({2} skipped).
Register in Behavior: {0} has no behbnd.
Register in Behavior: the behbnd of {0} has no behavior file.
Havok Editor: there is no binder named {0}.
Havok Editor: {1} has no file named {0}.
The behavior's events: where each one's transitions lead, and every field that sends or listens for it. Add, rename and delete events here.
Events a transition or another field of this file refers to.
Events nothing in this file refers to. A script (HKS) may still fire them, so they aren't necessarily safe to delete.
Events whose name another event of the file also has (the game's DS3 files have some).
Another event of this file has the same name. Anything that fires the event by name may reach either one.
Copy the selected events' names to the clipboard, one per line.
This file has no events. In Elden Ring and Nightreign a character's own behavior file has none: its events are in the binder's shared c9997.hkx (the player's are in c0000.hkx).
Show the binder's shared behavior file, which holds the events.
The event's name. Fields in this file refer to the event by its index, so they follow a rename.
Scripts (HKS) fire events by name, and in Dark Souls III the binder's other behavior files match events by name too. Those aren't checked: update them by hand after a rename.
The event's index in the behavior graph's event names, which the fields that refer to it hold.
The event's hkbEventInfo. Its flags are 0 on every event in the game's files.
Every field in this file that refers to the event: the transitions it triggers, and the fields that send or listen for it.
Nothing in this file reacts to this event. A script may still fire it.
Click to show the state the transition leads to in the Outline. Right-click to delete the transition.
Click to show the object in the Outline. Right-click to set the field to None.
Set this field to -1, so it no longer names the event (undoable).
Add an event at the end of the list (a name and an event info with flags 0, as every event in the game's files has).
It is added at index {0}. Add a transition on it with Add Transition.
Remove the selected events, the transitions on them, and set the other fields that name them to None. The events after them move down, and every index to them follows.
{0} other field(s) that name it are set to None (-1)
A state machine's return, random or next-state event becomes None.
Nothing in this file refers to it
The {0} event(s) after it move down; the fields that name them follow
Scripts (HKS) and other behavior files may fire these events by name. Those aren't checked.
Remove this transition (undoable). A state or machine left with no transitions holds none, as in the game's files.
Every behavior file of the shown behbnd.
Behavior files with unsaved changes, and saved files that differ from the game's copy or that the game doesn't have.
Every behavior file of every behbnd. Each one is read in the background, so this takes a while.
Open a behavior file to use this scope.
Only the first {0} results are listed.
{0} file(s) couldn't be read (hover for the list).
The behavior scan stopped with an error.
Click to show it. A result in another file opens that file first.
Couldn't find "{0}" in the file: it may have been edited since the search. Run it again.
Check every behavior file of the scope. Files with unsaved changes are checked as the editor has them, the others as stored.
Press Check to check the files of this scope.
Event names, with where each one's first transition leads.
Variable names, with their type and how many bindings use them.
Clips by animation name (a000_030000). A number, or a full animation name, also finds the selectors with that animation ID.
State names, with their state machine and state ID.
Any object with a matching m_name, with its type.
Match the whole name (ignoring case) instead of any part of it.
Search the files of the scope.
Saved {0} with {1} problem(s). See the Problems tool in the Behavior Editor.
Which behavior files the tool works on.
Run the tool on the files of the scope.
Find events, variables, animations, states or any named object in the behavior files.
What to search for, and the text to match.
What the search found. Click a result to show it; one in another file opens that file first.
Enter a name and press Search.
Check behavior files for the mistakes that make the game crash or silently do nothing: indices that name nothing, mismatched lists, duplicate state IDs, clip animation IDs and binding paths.
The problems found. Click one to show its object; one in another file opens that file first.
The state the new one is copied from: its selector, clips, outgoing transitions and the wildcard into it.
The new state's name, its selector's name, and the animation ID its clips play.
The new state's name. It gets state ID {0}, the next free one.
The name of the new state's animation selector (CustomManualSelectorGenerator).
The animation ID (m_animId). The copied clips play aCCC_ followed by this ID, keeping each clip's category.
This is the template's animation ID: the new state would play the same animations.
{0} other selector(s) in this file already use this animation ID.
How the new state is entered.
Add a transition from any state on an event
A wildcard transition into the new state, copied from the one into the template state (its flags, effect and intervals), on the event below.
The event that starts the action.
Scripts (HKS) fire the event by name: add it to the character's script by hand.
New Action: the action starts on event {0}. Add it to the character's script (HKS) to use it.
This selector isn't held by a state.
Add a move copied from this state: a new state playing a new animation, with an event and a transition into it, as one undo step.
The state plays a {0}, not an animation selector.
What the open behavior file adds, removes or changes against the game's copy, kept up to date as you edit. The lists colour the same entries. Changed values can be put back.
Reading the game's copy of the file, to compare it with this one (step {0} of {1}). The vanilla colours appear once it's done.
The game's copy of this file couldn't be read, so its changes can't be listed.
The game has no copy of this file: all of it is new.
Couldn't read the game's copy of {0}.
Each added, removed or changed event, variable or object. Expand one to see its changed fields.
No changes: the file matches the game's copy.
Click to show it. Expand it to see the changed fields.
Only in the game's copy: there is nothing to show in this file.
Put every changed value field of this entry back to the game's value, as one undo step. Structural changes stay.
Put this field back to the game's value (undoable). An event or variable field goes back to the same name.
The event or variable the game's field names isn't in this file any more, so the field can't be put back.
A reference or list length that differs. These are listed but not reverted.
No action script goes with this behavior file (none is named after it or its character).
Back to where the last jump came from.
The action scripts that go with this behavior file: the one named after it, and its character's own.
Where the script was read from: the project's copy, or the game's. A compiled script is shown decompiled; its line numbers are those of this text. The window is read only.
Read the scripts again, after changing them outside Smithbox.
Events the action scripts that go with this file name, e.g. in ExecEvent("W_...").
Events no paired action script names. The game fires many of these itself (W_Damage, W_Death, W_Fall ...), so this doesn't mean they're unused.
The scripts name {0} event(s) this file lacks (hover for the list)

W_ names in the paired action scripts with no event in this file. The game's own files have some (placeholders, cut content, and shared enemy scripts naming events only some characters have); after a rename or delete, the new ones show here.
Each line of the paired action scripts ({0}) that names this event. Click one to show it in the Script window.
No paired action script names this event. The game may still fire it itself.
Show this line in the Script window.
{0} name this event: after a rename, update them by hand (the Script window is read only). In Dark Souls III the binder's other behavior files match events by name too.
{0} names it on {1} line(s): update the script, or it will fire an event this file no longer has
Where {0} is defined. Click to show it in the Script window.
No paired action script defines {0}. A few of the game's own callbacks aren't defined either, so this may be harmless.
The copy is from {0} files and this file is {1}: objects can only be pasted between files of the same Havok version.
Events the pasted objects use that this file has no event of that name for. Ticked ones are added; the fields naming an unticked one are set to None.
Variables the pasted objects use that this file lacks. Ticked ones are added with the source's type, bounds and initial value; the bindings to an unticked one are dropped.
None: this file has them all.
What else the paste does to fit the objects into this file.
{0} character propert(ies) this file lacks can't be added: the bindings to them are dropped (hover for the list).
Animations this file's clips don't play yet: {0} (each gets an animation name entry, where the file has them)
Transition effects reused from this file by name: {0} (the others are copied)
Events and variables are matched by name. Everything is one undo step.
Pasted {0} object(s) from another file; added {1} event(s) and {2} variable(s).
Colour the transitions on events whose name contains this text, and the states they lead to. Wildcard transitions on them are drawn from the Any state node.
Centre the graph on the first state whose name contains this text, and select it.
Every modifier of the behavior (look-at, foot and hand IK, keyframe bones, jiggler ... and modifier lists), with what holds it. Enable, duplicate, delete and add modifiers here.
Show the modifiers of one type.
Switch m_enable: a disabled modifier doesn't run (undoable).
Add a copy right after it in its modifier list, named uniquely (undoable).
Remove it from its modifier list (undoable).
Add a copy of {0} at the end of this list: a modifier of this type as the game sets one up, to adjust.
Only a modifier in a modifier list can be duplicated or deleted.
{0} plays this modifier directly: deleting it would leave the generator without one. Change the generator's m_modifier instead.
Show each modifier generator's modifiers under it (a modifier list's entries below the list).
States, generators, clips and modifiers you bookmarked (right-click → Bookmark), in any behavior file. Kept with the project, not in the files.
Grouped by file, the shown file first. Click one to show it; one in another file opens that file first.
No bookmarks yet. Right-click a state, selector, clip, state machine or modifier and choose Bookmark.
Show this {0}. A bookmark finds its object by type and name, so it may not be found after the object is renamed.
Keep this object in the Bookmarks tool, to come back to it from any file. Kept with the project.
Couldn't read the behavior bookmarks from {0}.
Couldn't save the behavior bookmarks to {0}.
The categories (aCCC) of the selector's clips. In the game's files a selector has one clip per category, so pick one not listed.
Category {0} is taken: {1} plays it already
Use the category after the selector's highest, as Duplicate does.
The machine has {0} state(s), IDs up to {1}
A new state takes the ID after the machine's highest, so it never clashes with one in use (the game's IDs aren't always in order or without gaps).
